title.zh: 卷一百七十五 列傳第六十二: 張珪 李孟 張養浩 敬儼
title.en: Volume 175 Biographies 62: Zhang Gui, Li Meng, Zhang Yanghao, Jing Yan
title.raw: 卷一百七十五 列傳第六十二: 張珪 李孟 張養浩 敬儼 Volume 175 Biographies 62: Zhang Gui, Li Meng, Zhang Yanghao, Jing Yan

sentences.zh: 張珪，字公端，弘範之子也。

translations.literal: Zhang Gui, style name Gongduan, was a son of Hongfan.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Gui, courtesy name Gongduan, was the son of Hongfan.

sentences.zh: 少能挽強命中，嘗從其父出林中，有虎，珪抽矢直前，虎人立，洞其喉，一軍盡嘩。

translations.literal: In youth he could draw the stiff bow and hit the mark; once when following his father out into the forest there was a tiger — Gui drew an arrow and went straight forward; the tiger reared upright; he pierced its throat; the whole army shouted in acclaim.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth he could draw a heavy bow and strike true. Once when he followed his father into the woods, a tiger appeared. Gui nocked an arrow and charged straight at it; the tiger rose on its hind legs, and he drove the shaft through its throat. The whole army burst into cheers.

sentences.zh: 至元十六年，弘範平廣海，宋禮部侍郎鄧光薦將赴水死，弘範救而禮之，命珪受學。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan Hongfan pacified Guang and Hai; Song Ministry of Rites vice director Deng Guangjian was about to throw himself into the water and die; Hongfan rescued him and treated him with courtesy, and ordered Gui to receive instruction.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 16 Hongfan pacified the Guang and Hai region. Deng Guangjian, vice director of the Song Ministry of Rites, was about to drown himself; Hongfan saved him, received him with honor, and had Gui study under him.

sentences.zh: 光薦嘗遺一編書，目曰《相業》，語珪曰：「熟讀此，後必賴其用。

translations.literal: Guangjian once gave a book in one fascicle, its title "Statesmanship," and said to Gui: "Study this thoroughly — later you will surely rely on its use.
translations.idiomatic: Guangjian once presented him with a single fascicle entitled Statesmanship and told Gui, "Master this well; you will surely need it hereafter.

sentences.zh: 」師還，道出江淮，珪年十六，攝管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: " When the army returned, the route passed Jianghuai; Gui was sixteen and acted as regent commander of the army wanhu.
translations.idiomatic: " When the troops marched home by way of the Jianghuai region, Gui was sixteen and served as acting commander of the ten-thousand-household army.

sentences.zh: 十七年，真拜昭勇大將軍、管軍萬戶，佩其父虎符，治所統軍，鎮建康。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was formally appointed General of Manifest Valor and wanhu in command of troops, wore his father's tiger tally, administered the troops under his command, and garrisoned Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: In year 17 he received formal appointment as General of Manifest Valor and commander of the ten-thousand-household army, bearing his father's tiger tally. He took charge of his command and was posted to garrison Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 未幾，弘範卒，喪畢，世祖召見，親撫之。

translations.literal: Before long Hongfan died; when mourning was finished Shizu summoned him for audience and personally comforted him.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Hongfan died. When the mourning period ended, Kublai Khan summoned him to court and comforted him in person.

sentences.zh: 奏曰：「臣年幼，軍事重，聶禎者，從臣父、祖，久歷行陣，幸以副臣。

translations.literal: He memorialized: "Your subject is young and military affairs are weighty; Nie Zhen has followed my father and grandfather, long experienced in campaigning — I beg he assist your subject.
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized, "Your subject is young and military affairs are grave. Nie Zhen has served my father and grandfather and is long practiced in the field — I beg that he be appointed to assist me.

sentences.zh: 」帝歎曰：「求老成自副，常兒不知出此。

translations.literal: " The Emperor sighed and said: "Seeking an elder statesman as one's deputy — ordinary boys do not think of this.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor sighed and said, "To seek a seasoned man as one's deputy — an ordinary lad would never think of that.

sentences.zh: 」厚賜而遣之，遍及其從者。

translations.literal: " He richly rewarded him and sent him off, extending rewards to all who accompanied him.
translations.idiomatic: " He gave him rich gifts and sent him away, extending rewards to everyone in his retinue.

sentences.zh: 十九年，太平、宣、徽群盜起，行省檄珪討之，士卒數為賊所敗，卒有殺民家豕而並傷其主者，珪曰：「此軍之所以敗也。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year bandits rose in masses in Taiping, Xuan, and Hui; the branch secretariat ordered Gui to suppress them; the soldiers were repeatedly defeated by bandits; once a soldier killed a commoner's pig and also wounded its owner; Gui said: "This is why the army is defeated.
translations.idiomatic: In year 19 bandit gangs rose in Taiping, Xuan, and Hui. The branch secretariat ordered Gui to suppress them. His troops suffered repeated defeats, and once a soldier killed a peasant's pig and wounded its owner as well. Gui said, "This is why an army loses.

sentences.zh: 」斬其卒，悉平諸盜。

translations.literal: " He beheaded that soldier and completely pacified all bandits.
translations.idiomatic: " He executed that soldier and fully pacified the bandits.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，入朝。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year he came to court.
translations.idiomatic: In year 29 he came to court.

sentences.zh: 時朝廷言者謂天下事定，行樞密院可罷；

translations.literal: At the time court speakers said the realm was settled and the traveling Secretariat of Military Affairs could be abolished;
translations.idiomatic: At the time memorialists at court said the empire was settled and the itinerant Bureau of Military Affairs could be abolished;

sentences.zh: 江浙行省參知政事張瑄，領海道，亦以為言。

translations.literal: Zhang Xuan, Jiangzhe branch secretariat associate administrator in charge of the sea route, also spoke to that effect.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Xuan, associate administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat in charge of the sea route, said the same.

sentences.zh: 樞密副使暗伯問於珪，珪曰：「見上當自言之。

translations.literal: Vice director of the Secretariat Anbo asked Gui; Gui said: "When you see the Sovereign you should speak for yourself.
translations.idiomatic: Vice director of the Secretariat Anbo asked Gui about it. Gui said, "When you see His Majesty, you should speak for yourself.

sentences.zh: 」召對，珪曰：「縱使行院可罷，亦非宣所宜言。

translations.literal: " Called for audience, Gui said: "Even if the traveling yamen could be abolished, it is still not something Xuan should have said.
translations.idiomatic: " Summoned to audience, Gui said, "Even if the traveling bureau could be abolished, that was still not something Xuan ought to have said.

sentences.zh: 」遂得不罷。

translations.literal: " Thus it was not abolished.
translations.idiomatic: " The bureau was therefore not abolished.

sentences.zh: 命為樞密副使。

translations.literal: He was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 太傅月兒魯那演言：「珪尚少，姑試以僉書，果可大用，請俟他日。

translations.literal: Grand tutor Yehülü Nayen said: "Gui is still young — for the moment try him as director-general; if he proves fit for great use, please wait for another day.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Tutor Yehülü Nayen said, "Gui is still young; for now try him as director-general. If he truly proves fit for high office, let us wait for another day.

sentences.zh: 」帝曰：「不然，是家為國滅金、滅宋，盡死力者三世矣，而可吝此耶！

translations.literal: " The Emperor said: "Not so — this house for the state destroyed Jin and destroyed Song, exhausting strength through three generations; can we begrudge this!
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said, "No. This family has for three generations given their lives to destroy Jin and Song for the state — and we would stint this reward?

sentences.zh: 」拜鎮國上將軍、江淮行樞密副使。

translations.literal: " He was appointed General for the Pacification of the State and vice director of the Jianghuai traveling Secretariat of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: " He was appointed General for the Pacification of the State and vice director of the Jianghuai itinerant Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 成宗即位，行院罷。

translations.literal: When Chengzong took the throne the traveling yamen was abolished.
translations.idiomatic: When Temür acceded, the itinerant bureau was abolished.

sentences.zh: 大德三年，遣使巡行天下，珪使川、陝，問民疾苦，賑恤孤貧，罷冗官，黜貪吏。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade emissaries were dispatched to tour the realm; Gui was sent to Sichuan and Shaanxi, inquiring into the people's hardships, relieving the orphaned and poor, abolishing superfluous offices, and dismissing corrupt officials.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 3 envoys were sent to tour the empire. Gui was assigned to Sichuan and Shaanxi, where he inquired into the people's hardships, relieved the orphaned and destitute, abolished redundant offices, and removed corrupt officials.

sentences.zh: 還，擢江南行御史臺侍御史，換文階中奉大夫，遷浙西肅政廉訪使。

translations.literal: On return he was promoted to supervising censor of the Jiangnan branch censorate, exchanged to civil rank Grand Master of Proper Submission, and transferred to Jiangxi surveillance commissioner for rectifying conduct.
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was promoted to supervising censor of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate, exchanged to the civil rank of Grand Master of Proper Submission, and transferred to surveillance commissioner for rectifying conduct in western Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 劾罷郡長吏以下三十餘人、府史胥徒數百，徵贓巨萬計。

translations.literal: He impeached and removed more than thirty prefectural administrators and below, several hundred clerks and runners, and recovered illicit funds amounting to tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached and removed more than thirty prefects and lower officials, along with several hundred clerks and runners, and recovered illicit gains amounting to tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 珪得鹽司姦利事，將發之。

translations.literal: Gui obtained evidence of the salt bureau's illicit profits and was about to expose it.
translations.idiomatic: Gui uncovered evidence of corruption in the salt administration and was about to expose it.

sentences.zh: 事幹行省，有內不自安者，欲以危法中珪，賂遺近臣，妄言珪有厭勝事，且沮鹽法。

translations.literal: The affair involved the branch secretariat; some ill at ease within sought to destroy Gui by legal peril, bribing close attendants, falsely saying Gui practiced sorcery against the court and also obstructed the salt law.
translations.idiomatic: The case implicated the branch secretariat. Men who felt themselves endangered tried to destroy Gui with the law, bribing court favorites to claim falsely that he had practiced sorcery against the throne and had obstructed the salt monopoly.

sentences.zh: 帝遣官雜治之，得行省大小吏及鹽官欺罔狀，皆伏罪。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent officials to investigate jointly; deception by great and petty officials of the branch secretariat and salt officials was obtained; all confessed guilt.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent officials to investigate jointly. The fraud of high and low officials in the branch secretariat and in the salt offices was exposed, and all confessed.

sentences.zh: 召珪拜僉樞密院事，入見，賜只孫冠服侍宴，又命買宅以賜，辭不受。

translations.literal: Gui was summoned and appointed director of the Secretariat; on entering audience he was granted a jisun hat and robe and entertained at banquet; he was also ordered to buy a residence to grant him but declined and did not accept.
translations.idiomatic: Gui was summoned and appointed director of the Secretariat. At audience he was given a jisun cap and robe and entertained at banquet; the court also ordered a house bought for him as a gift, but he declined and would not accept.

sentences.zh: 拜江南行台御史中丞，因上疏，極言天人之際、災異之故，其目有修德行、廣言路、進君子、退小人、信賞必罰、減冗官、節浮費，以法祖宗成憲，累數百言。

translations.literal: He was appointed director of the Jiangnan branch censorate and submitted a memorial vigorously expounding the relation between Heaven and man and the causes of prodigies — its items included cultivating virtue, broadening channels of remonstrance, advancing gentlemen and retiring petty men, trusting rewards and certain punishment, reducing superfluous offices, and curbing extravagant expenditure, to follow the established statutes of the ancestors — altogether several hundred words.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed director of the Jiangnan Branch Censorate and submitted a memorial that spoke at length on the relation between Heaven and humankind and the causes of strange portents. Its headings included cultivating virtue, widening avenues of remonstrance, advancing worthy men and removing petty men, making rewards sure and punishments certain, cutting redundant offices, and restraining wasteful spending — all to follow the settled precedents of the founding ancestors — running to several hundred words.

sentences.zh: 劾大官之不法者，不報；

translations.literal: He impeached great officials who acted unlawfully; no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached high officials who violated the law, but received no response.

sentences.zh: 並及近侍之熒惑者，又不報。

translations.literal: He also impeached close attendants who misled the ruler; again no reply.
translations.idiomatic: He also impeached palace intimates who misled the throne; again there was no response.

sentences.zh: 遂謝病歸。

translations.literal: Thereupon he took leave on grounds of illness and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon he resigned on grounds of illness and went home.

sentences.zh: 久之，拜陝西行台中丞，不赴。

translations.literal: After a long while he was appointed director of the Shaanxi branch censorate but did not take up the post.
translations.idiomatic: After a long interval he was appointed director of the Shaanxi Branch Censorate, but he did not take up the appointment.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，拜榮祿大夫、樞密副使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and vice director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he was appointed Grand Master for Glorious Blessing and vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 徽政院使失列門請以洪城軍隸興聖宮，而己領之，以上旨移文樞密院，眾恐懼承命，珪固不署，事遂不行。

translations.literal: Director of the Bureau of Palace Attendants Shilie'men requested that Hongcheng Army be placed under the Consecration Palace while he himself would lead it; citing the sovereign's intent he sent a document to the Secretariat; everyone feared and would obey the order; Gui firmly refused to sign and the matter did not go through.
translations.idiomatic: Shilie'men, director of the Bureau of Palace Attendants, asked that the Hongcheng Army be placed under the Consecration Palace while he himself would command it. Citing the sovereign's intent, he sent an order to the Secretariat. Everyone was afraid and ready to comply, but Gui steadfastly refused to sign, and the matter was dropped.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，拜中書平章政事，請減煩冗還有司，以清政務，得專修宰相之職，帝從之，著為令。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou he was appointed associate administrator of the central secretariat; he requested reducing troublesome superfluity and returning matters to the responsible offices to clarify government affairs, so that one might devote oneself solely to the duties of chancellor — the Emperor assented and this was enacted as an ordinance.
translations.idiomatic: In Yanyou 2 he was appointed associate administrator of the Central Secretariat. He asked that vexatious redundancies be cut back and returned to the proper agencies so that government might be clarified and the chancellor could devote himself solely to the duties of office. The emperor agreed, and this was written into law.

sentences.zh: 教坊使曹咬住拜禮部尚書，珪曰：「伶人為宗伯，何以示後世！

translations.literal: Court entertainer Cao Yaozhu was appointed Minister of Rites; Gui said: "A player as chief of ceremonies — how can this be shown to posterity!
translations.idiomatic: The court entertainer Cao Yaozhu was appointed Minister of Rites. Gui said, "To make an actor chief of ceremonies — what lesson is that for posterity?

sentences.zh: 」力諫止之。

translations.literal: " He remonstrated with all his strength and stopped it.
translations.idiomatic: " He remonstrated with all his force and stopped the appointment.

sentences.zh: 皇太后以中書右丞相鐵木迭兒為太師，萬戶別薛參知行省政事，珪曰：「太師論道經邦，鐵木迭兒非其人，別薛無功，不得為外執政。

translations.literal: The empress dowager wished to appoint right chancellor Temür Ogedei as Grand Tutor and wanhu Biexie as associate administrator of branch secretariat affairs; Gui said: "The Grand Tutor discusses the Way and orders the state — Temür Ogedei is not the man; Biexie has no merit and may not serve as external administrator.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager wished to appoint the right chancellor Temür Ogedei as Grand Tutor and the wanhu Biexie as associate administrator of branch secretariat affairs. Gui said, "The Grand Tutor is to expound the Way and govern the realm. Temür Ogedei is not that man. Biexie has no merit and must not hold provincial power.

sentences.zh: 」車駕度居庸，失列門傳皇太后旨，召珪切責，杖之。

translations.literal: " When the imperial carriage crossed Juyong Pass, Shilie'men transmitted the empress dowager's order, summoned Gui, and sternly reproached him; he was beaten with the staff.
translations.idiomatic: " As the imperial carriage crossed Juyong Pass, Shilie'men conveyed the empress dowager's order, summoned Gui, and rebuked him sharply; he was beaten with the rod.

sentences.zh: 珪創甚，輿歸京師，明日遂出國門。

translations.literal: Gui's wound was severe; he was carried back to the capital, and the next day left the capital gate.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's injuries were grave. He was carried back to the capital, and the next day left the city gate.

sentences.zh: 珪子景元掌符璽，不得一日去宿衛，至是，以父病篤告，遽歸。

translations.literal: Gui's son Jingyuan held the seals and could not for a single day leave palace guard duty; on this occasion, reporting that his father's illness was critical, he hurried home.
translations.idiomatic: Gui's son Jingyuan held the imperial seals and could not leave palace guard duty for a single day. On this occasion he reported that his father was gravely ill and rushed home.

sentences.zh: 帝驚曰：「鄉別時，卿父無病。

translations.literal: The Emperor was startled and said: "When we parted, your father had no illness.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was startled and said, "When we parted, your father was not ill.

sentences.zh: 」景元頓首涕泣，不敢言。

translations.literal: " Jingyuan knocked his head and wept but dared not speak.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingyuan kowtowed and wept but dared not speak.

sentences.zh: 帝不懌，遣參議中書省事換住往賜之酒，遂拜大司徒，謝病家居。

translations.literal: The Emperor was displeased; he sent Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat Huanzhu to go and grant wine; thereupon he was appointed Grand Minister of State and took leave on grounds of illness to dwell at home.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was displeased. He sent Associate Administrator of the Central Secretariat Huanzhu to present wine as a gift. Gui was then appointed Grand Minister of State and retired on grounds of illness to live at home.

sentences.zh: 繼丁母憂，廬墓寢苫啜粥者三年。

translations.literal: Subsequently he entered mourning for his mother; at the grave he lived in a hut, slept on brushwood, and drank gruel for three years.
translations.idiomatic: He later entered mourning for his mother. At her grave he lived in a hut, slept on brushwood, and took only thin gruel for three years.

sentences.zh: 六年七月，帝憶珪生日，賜上尊、御衣。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the sixth year the Emperor remembered Gui's birthday and granted superior wine and imperial robes.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of year 6 the emperor remembered Gui's birthday and sent superior wine and imperial robes.

sentences.zh: 至治二年，英宗召見於易水之上曰：「四世舊臣，朕將畀卿以政。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizhi, Yingzong summoned him above the Yishui and said: "A minister through four generations — I shall entrust governance to you.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 2, Emperor Yingzong summoned him to the banks of the Yishui and said, "You are a minister of four generations; I mean to entrust you with government.

sentences.zh: 」珪辭歸。

translations.literal: " Gui declined and returned.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui declined and went home.

sentences.zh: 遣近臣設醴。

translations.literal: The Emperor sent close attendants to set out a feast.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent close attendants to set out a feast for him.

sentences.zh: 丞相拜住問珪曰：「宰相之體何先？

translations.literal: Chancellor Bayan asked Gui: "What comes first in the bearing of a chancellor?
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayan asked Gui, "What should come first in the conduct of a chief minister?

sentences.zh: 」珪曰：「莫先於格君心，莫急於廣言路。

translations.literal: " Gui said: "Nothing comes before rectifying the ruler's heart; nothing is more urgent than broadening the channels of remonstrance.
translations.idiomatic: " Gui said, "Nothing comes before rectifying the ruler's mind, and nothing is more urgent than opening the way for candid speech.

sentences.zh: 」是年冬，起珪為集賢大學士。

translations.literal: " That winter Gui was raised as grand academician of the Hall of Worthies.
translations.idiomatic: " That winter Gui was recalled as grand academician of the Hall of Worthies.

sentences.zh: 先是，鐵木迭兒既復為丞相，以私怨殺平章蕭拜住、御史中丞楊朵兒只、上都留守賀伯顏，大小之臣，不能自保。

translations.literal: Earlier Temür Ogedei had again become chancellor; out of private resentment he killed associate administrator Xiao Baizhu, censor in chief Yang Duo'erzhi, and Shangdu defender He Boyan — ministers great and small could not protect themselves.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Temür Ogedei had again become chancellor. Out of private resentment he had associate administrator Xiao Baizhu, censor-in-chief Yang Duo'erzhi, and Shangdu defender He Boyan put to death, and officials great and small could not protect themselves.

sentences.zh: 會地震風烈，敕廷臣集議弭災之道，珪抗言於坐曰：「弭災，當究其所以致災者。

translations.literal: When earthquake and violent winds occurred, the court ordered ministers to assemble and discuss ways to quell the calamity; Gui spoke defiantly at the gathering: "To quell calamity one must investigate what caused the calamity.
translations.idiomatic: When earthquakes and violent winds struck, the court ordered the ministers to meet and discuss how to allay the disaster. Gui spoke boldly in the assembly: "To allay a disaster one must find what caused it.

sentences.zh: 漢殺孝婦，三年不雨；

translations.literal: Under Han — when Xiaoji was killed — rain did not fall for three years;
translations.idiomatic: Under the Han, when the filial daughter was killed unjustly, rain failed for three years;

sentences.zh: 蕭、楊、賀冤死，非致沴之端乎！

translations.literal: Xiao, Yang, and He died wrongfully — are these not the beginnings that produce baleful influence!
translations.idiomatic: Xiao, Yang, and He were killed unjustly — are these not the very sources of such ill omens?

sentences.zh: 死者固不可復生，而情義猶可昭白，毋使朝廷終失之也。

translations.literal: The dead certainly cannot live again, but right and principle may still be made clear — let not the court ultimately lose them.
translations.idiomatic: The dead cannot be revived, but justice can still be made clear. Let the court not abandon them forever.

sentences.zh: 」又拜中書平章政事，侍宴萬壽山，賜以五帶。

translations.literal: He was again appointed associate administrator of the central secretariat; at a banquet on Longevity Mount he was granted the five zones of the belt.
translations.idiomatic: He was again appointed associate administrator of the Central Secretariat. At a banquet on Longevity Mount he was granted the five-zone belt.

sentences.zh: 三年秋八月，御史大夫鐵失既行殺逆，夜入都門，坐中書堂，矯制奪執符印，珪密疏言：「賊黨罪不可逭。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of autumn of the third year, censor in chief Tieshi, having carried out regicide, entered the capital gate by night, sat in the central secretariat hall, and by forged edict seized and held the tallies and seals; Gui submitted a secret memorial saying: "The faction of traitors — their crime cannot be pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of autumn in year 3, Censor-in-Chief Tieshi, having committed regicide, entered the capital gate by night, sat in the Central Secretariat hall, and by forged edict seized the tallies and seals. Gui submitted a secret memorial: "The traitor faction must not be spared.

sentences.zh: 」既皆伏誅，鐵木迭兒之子治書侍御史鎖南，獨議遠流，珪曰：「於法，強盜不分首從，發塚傷尸者亦死。

translations.literal: After all had been executed, Temür Ogedei's son Suonam, supervising secretary of the Secretariat, alone argued for exile to a distant place; Gui said: "By law, in robbery there is no distinction of ringleader and follower; those who open graves and harm corpses are also put to death.
translations.idiomatic: After the culprits were executed, Temür Ogedei's son Suonam, supervising secretary of the Secretariat, alone argued for exile. Gui said, "By law, robbers are punished alike whether chief or follower, and those who open graves and mutilate corpses are also put to death.

sentences.zh: 鎖南從弒逆，親斫丞相拜住臂，乃欲活之耶！

translations.literal: Suonam followed the regicide — he personally hacked Chancellor Bayan's arm — yet you would keep him alive!
translations.idiomatic: Suonam took part in the regicide and personally hacked Chancellor Bayan's arm — and you would let him live?

sentences.zh: 」遂伏誅。

translations.literal: Thereupon he was executed.
translations.idiomatic: Suonam was thereupon executed.

sentences.zh: 盜竊仁廟神主，時參知政事馬剌兼領太常禮儀使，當遷左丞，珪曰：「以參政遷左丞，姑曰敘進。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets of Renzong's temple were stolen; at the time Associate Administrator Mara concurrently held the post of director of imperial rites and was to be transferred to left vice director; Gui said: "To transfer from associate administrator to left vice director may be called sequential promotion.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets in Renzong's temple were stolen. At the time Associate Administrator Mara also held the post of director of imperial rites and was to be promoted to left vice director. Gui said, "To move from associate administrator to left vice director might be called routine promotion.

sentences.zh: 而太常奉宗祏不謹，當待罪，而反遷官，何以謝在天之靈！

translations.literal: But the Directorate of Imperial Rites did not reverently guard the ancestral tablets — he should await punishment; yet instead he is promoted — how may we answer the spirits in Heaven!
translations.idiomatic: Yet the Directorate of Imperial Rites failed to guard the ancestral tablets with due reverence — he ought to await punishment, not receive promotion. How can we answer the spirits in Heaven?

sentences.zh: 」命遂不下。

translations.literal: The order was thereupon not issued.
translations.idiomatic: The appointment was therefore not issued.

sentences.zh: 國之安危，在乎論相。

translations.literal: A state's safety or danger lies in the selection of chancellors.
translations.idiomatic: Whether a state stands or falls depends on whom it appoints as chancellor.

sentences.zh: 昔唐玄宗前用姚崇、宋璟則治，後用李林甫、楊國忠，天下騷動，幾致亡國。

translations.literal: Formerly Tang Xuanzong first used Yao Chong and Song Jing and had order; later he used Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong — the realm was in turmoil and nearly perished.
translations.idiomatic: In Tang times, Emperor Xuanzong first employed Yao Chong and Song Jing and the realm was well governed; later he employed Li Linfu and Yang Guozhong, and the empire was thrown into turmoil and nearly perished.

sentences.zh: 雖賴子儀諸將，效忠竭力，克復舊物，然自是籓鎮縱橫，紀綱亦不復振矣。

translations.literal: Although he relied on Guo Ziyi and other generals who loyally strove with all their strength to recover the former realm, from that time regional commanders ran rampant and discipline could no longer be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Although he then relied on Guo Ziyi and other generals who served loyally and with all their strength recovered the old territories, from that time the military governors grew unruly and central discipline was never restored.

sentences.zh: 良由李林甫石害忠良，佈置邪黨，姦惑蒙蔽，保祿養禍所致，死有餘辜。

translations.literal: Truly because Li Linfu wielded power to harm the loyal and good, placed wicked factions, deceived and blinded with flattery, preserved salary and nourished calamity — when dead he still had guilt to spare.
translations.idiomatic: This was truly because Li Linfu abused power to destroy the loyal and worthy, planted wicked factions, and deluded the court with flattery while hoarding office and nurturing disaster — crimes for which death itself was not enough.

sentences.zh: 如前宰相鐵木迭兒，奸狡險深，陰謀叢出，專政十年。

translations.literal: Such as the former chancellor Temür Ogedei — crafty, deceitful, deep and sinister, conspiracies issuing in clusters, monopolizing government for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: The former chancellor Temür Ogedei was of the same kind: treacherous, deceitful, deep and insidious, plotting incessantly, and monopolizing power for ten years.

sentences.zh: 凡宗戚忤己者，巧飾危間，陰中以法，忠直被誅竄者甚眾。

translations.literal: All imperial kinsmen who opposed him he artfully dressed with deadly slander and secretly struck with the law; the upright and loyal who were executed and banished were very many.
translations.idiomatic: All members of the imperial clan who crossed him he ensnared with fabricated charges and destroyed by law in secret; the upright and loyal who were executed or banished were very many.

sentences.zh: 始以贓敗，諂附權奸失列門，及嬖幸也裡失班之徒，苟全其生，尋任太子太師。

translations.literal: At first he was defeated for corruption, fawned on and attached to the power-minister Shilie'men and favorites such as Yelü Shiban — barely preserving his life — then soon he was appointed Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At first he was ruined by corruption, then fawned on the power-holder Shilie'men and favorites such as Yelü Shiban and barely saved his life; soon afterward he was made Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 未幾，仁宗賓天，乘時幸變，再入中書。

translations.literal: Before long Renzong passed away; seizing the moment of fortunate change, he again entered the central secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Before long Renzong died. Seizing the moment of upheaval, he entered the Central Secretariat again.

sentences.zh: 當英廟之初，與失列門等恩義相許，表里為姦，誣殺蕭、楊等，以快私怨。

translations.literal: When Yingzong first acceded, he and Shilie'men and others had pledged mutual favor — inside and outside they were partners in wickedness — falsely killed Xiao and Yang and others to satisfy private resentment.
translations.idiomatic: When Yingzong first took the throne, he and Shilie'men and the rest had pledged mutual support; inside and outside the court they acted as partners in evil and had Xiao, Yang, and the others killed on false charges to satisfy private grudges.

sentences.zh: 天討元凶，失列門之黨既誅，坐要上功，遂獲信任，諸子內布宿衛，外據顯要，蔽上抑下，杜絕言路，賣官鬻獄，威福己出，一令發口，上下股栗，稍不附己，其禍立至，權勢日熾，中外寒心。

translations.literal: Heaven punished the chief culprit; Shilie'men's faction was executed; sitting for merit on high he thereupon gained trust; his sons were stationed within as palace guards and held eminent posts without — blocking the sovereign and suppressing those below, cutting off all channels of speech, selling offices and peddling judgments, authority and blessing issuing from himself — one order from his mouth and above and below trembled in the thighs; those slightly not attached to him met disaster at once; his power daily waxed hot and within and without were heartsick.
translations.idiomatic: Heaven punished the chief culprit when Shilie'men's faction was executed, yet Temür Ogedei, claiming credit, won trust again. His sons held palace guard posts within and high offices without; they blocked the throne, crushed those below, and shut every avenue of speech. They sold offices and traded judgments; power and favor flowed from him alone. One word from his mouth and the court trembled; anyone who did not attach himself to him was ruined at once. His authority grew daily hotter, and everyone within and without the court despaired.

sentences.zh: 由是群邪並進，如逆賊鐵失之徒，名為義子，實其腹心，忠良屏跡，坐待收系。

translations.literal: Thereupon the wicked advanced together — such traitors as Tieshi, nominally called adopted sons, were in truth his trusted inner circle; the loyal and good were screened off, sitting and awaiting arrest.
translations.idiomatic: Then the wicked advanced together. Men such as the traitor Tieshi were called his adopted sons in name but were in fact his trusted inner circle. The loyal and worthy were driven aside, waiting only to be seized.

sentences.zh: 先帝悟其奸惡，僕碑奪爵，籍沒其家，終以遺患，構成弒逆。

translations.literal: The late emperor perceived his wickedness — his stele was cast down and his fief confiscated — yet in the end he left a lingering harm that formed regicide.
translations.idiomatic: The late emperor saw his wickedness, cast down his memorial stele, and confiscated his household, yet in the end the harm he left behind led to regicide.

sentences.zh: 其子鎖南，親與逆謀，所由來者漸矣，雖剖棺戮屍，夷滅其家，猶不足以塞責。

translations.literal: His son Suonam personally joined the treasonous plot — the source of this was gradual; though the coffin be opened and the corpse flogged and the family exterminated root and branch, it still would not suffice to answer for the crime.
translations.idiomatic: His son Suonam personally joined the plot of treason. The disaster came by degrees. Even opening his coffin, flogging his corpse, and exterminating his house root and branch would not be enough to atone.

sentences.zh: 今復回給所籍家產，諸子尚在京師，夤緣再入宿衛。

translations.literal: Now his confiscated household property is returned; his sons are still in the capital, currying favor to re-enter palace guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Now his confiscated property is being returned, and his sons remain in the capital, scheming by connections to re-enter palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 世祖時，阿合馬貪殘敗事，雖死猶正其罪，況如鐵木迭兒之奸惡者哉！

translations.literal: In Shizu's time Ahama was greedy and corrupt and ruined affairs; though dead his crime was still rectified — how much more Temür Ogedei's wickedness!
translations.idiomatic: In Kublai's reign Ahama was greedy and corrupt and ruined the state; though dead, his crimes were still punished. How much more Temür Ogedei's wickedness!

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜遵成憲，仍籍鐵木迭兒家產，遠竄其子孫​​外郡，以懲大奸。

translations.literal: We your subjects propose: follow the established statutes, again confiscate Temür Ogedei's household property, and exile his sons and grandsons to distant prefectures to punish great treachery.
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects propose: follow established precedent, confiscate Temür Ogedei's property again, and exile his sons and grandsons to distant prefectures, so that great treachery may be punished.

sentences.zh: 君父之仇，不共戴天，所以明綱常、別上下也。

translations.literal: The sovereign and father's enemy may not live under the same sky — thereby is normal principle clarified and high and low distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: One cannot live under the same sky as the enemy of one's ruler and father — by this the moral order is upheld and high and low are distinguished.

sentences.zh: 鐵失之黨，結謀弒逆，君相遇害，天下之人，痛心疾首，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: Tieshi's faction conspired in regicide; the ruler and lord met harm — people throughout the realm are heartsick and aggrieved; what they cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Tieshi's faction plotted regicide; the sovereign was murdered. All under Heaven are heartsick with grief — it is what none can bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 比奉旨：「以鐵失之徒既伏其辜，諸王按梯不花、孛羅、月魯鐵木兒、曲呂不花、兀魯思不花，亦已流竄，逆黨脅從者眾，何可盡誅。

translations.literal: Recently an edict: "Since Tieshi's party have paid their penalty, the princes Atipembuhua, Boluo, Yülü Temür, Qulübuhua, and Ulusibuhua have also been banished; the coerced followers of the traitorous faction are many — how can all be executed.
translations.idiomatic: A recent edict said: "Since Tieshi's party have already paid the penalty, and the princes Atipembuhua, Boluo, Yülü Temür, Qulübuhua, and Ulusibuhua have also been banished, the coerced followers of the traitor faction are many — how can all be put to death?

sentences.zh: 後之言事者，其勿復舉。

translations.literal: " Let speakers hereafter not raise the matter again.
translations.idiomatic: " Let memorialists hereafter not raise the matter again."

sentences.zh: 」臣等議：古法，弒逆，凡在官者殺無赦。

translations.literal: We your subjects propose: by ancient law, in regicide all who hold office are executed without pardon.
translations.idiomatic: We your subjects propose: by ancient law, in cases of regicide all who hold office are executed without pardon.

sentences.zh: 聖朝立法，強盜劫殺庶民，其同情者猶且首從俱罪，況弒逆之黨，天地不容，宜誅按梯不花之徒，以謝天下。

translations.literal: Our dynasty's law: in robbery and slaughter of common people, those of like mind are still punished principal and follower alike — how much more the regicidal faction, whom Heaven and earth will not contain — Atipembuhua's party should be executed to answer the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty's law: even in robbery and killing of commoners, those who share the intent are punished alike as principals and accomplices — how much less may the regicide faction, whom Heaven and earth cannot tolerate, go unpunished? Atipembuhua's party should be executed to answer the realm.

sentences.zh: 《書》曰：惟辟作福，惟辟作威。

translations.literal: The Documents says: Only the sovereign makes blessings, only the sovereign makes majesty.
translations.idiomatic: The Documents says: Only the sovereign bestows blessings; only the sovereign wields majesty.

sentences.zh: 臣無有作福作威，臣而有作福作威，害於而家，凶於而國。

translations.literal: Your subjects have no making blessings or making majesty; if subjects make blessings and make majesty, harmful to your house, baleful to your state.
translations.idiomatic: Subjects must not bestow blessings or wield majesty. If subjects do so, it harms your house and brings disaster on your state.

sentences.zh: 蓋生殺與奪，於子之權，非臣下所得盜用也。

translations.literal: For life and death, confiscation and bestowal belong to the Son's authority — not something subjects may usurp.
translations.idiomatic: The power of life and death, confiscation and reward, belongs to the Son of Heaven — not something subjects may usurp.

sentences.zh: 遼王脫脫，位冠宗室，居鎮遼東，屬任非輕，國家不幸，有非常之變，不能討賊，而乃覬幸赦恩，報復仇忿，殺親王妃主百餘人，分其羊馬畜產，殘忍骨肉，盜竊主權，聞者切齒。

translations.literal: Liao Prince Toto, standing above the imperial clan, garrisoning Liaodong — his trust was no light charge; the state was unlucky and had an abnormal change; he could not punish the traitors yet hoped for amnesty in his favor, avenging private hatred — killed more than a hundred of his kinsmen's wives and princesses, divided their sheep, horses, and livestock, cruel to flesh and bone, usurped the lord's authority — listeners gnashed teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Toto of Liao, foremost in the imperial clan and posted to garrison Liaodong, bore a weighty trust. When the state suffered this unnatural calamity he failed to punish the traitors; instead he looked for pardon and favor, avenged private hatred, and killed more than a hundred wives and princesses of his own kin, seizing their sheep, horses, and herds. He was cruel to his own flesh and blood and usurped the sovereign's authority — all who heard of it gnashed their teeth.

sentences.zh: 今不之罪，乃復厚賜放還，仍守爵土，臣恐國之紀綱，由此不振。

translations.literal: Now he is not punished but richly rewarded and sent back, still keeping his fief — we fear the state's discipline will thereby fail to be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Now he is not punished but richly rewarded and sent home, still holding his fief. We fear the state's discipline will never be restored.

sentences.zh: 設或效尤，何法以治！

translations.literal: If others imitate, by what law may we govern!
translations.idiomatic: If others follow his example, by what law can we govern?

sentences.zh: 且遼東地廣，素號重鎮，若使脫脫久居，彼既縱肆，將無忌憚，況令死者含冤，感傷和氣！

translations.literal: Moreover Liaodong's territory is broad, long known as a key post — if Toto dwells there long, he having been unrestrained will be without fear; moreover let the dead hold grievance and harm harmonious qi!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover Liaodong is vast and has long been a strategic region. If Toto remains there long, a man already so unrestrained will fear nothing. And how can the dead bear their grievance without harming the harmony of Heaven and earth?

sentences.zh: 臣等議：累朝典憲，聞赦殺人，罪在不原，宜奪削其爵土，置之他所，以彰天威。

translations.literal: We propose: according to the statutes of successive reigns, pardon does not extend to murderers — his fief should be seized and he placed elsewhere to display Heaven's awe.
translations.idiomatic: We propose: by the statutes of successive reigns, murderers are not pardoned. His fief should be seized and he should be placed elsewhere, to display Heaven's awe.

sentences.zh: 刑以懲惡，國有常憲。

translations.literal: Punishment is to chastise wickedness; the state has constant statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Punishment exists to chastise the wicked; the state has fixed laws.

sentences.zh: 武備卿即烈，前太尉不花，以累朝待遇之隆，俱致高列，不思補報，專務姦欺，詐稱奉旨，令鷹師強收鄭國寶妻古哈，貪其家人畜產，自恃權貴，莫敢如何。

translations.literal: Military Supplies Director Jilie and former Grand Marshal Buhua — because of the dynasty's generous treatment both reached high rank — did not think to repay but devoted themselves to wicked deception; falsely claiming to act by edict they ordered falconers forcibly to take Zheng Guobao's wife Guha; coveting her household's livestock they relied on their noble authority and none dared what to do.
translations.idiomatic: Military Supplies Director Jilie and former Grand Marshal Buhua had both risen to high rank through the dynasty's generous favor, yet instead of repaying it they devoted themselves to wicked fraud. They falsely claimed an imperial order and had falconers seize Zheng Guobao's wife Guha by force, coveting her family's livestock. Relying on their exalted rank, they acted as they pleased and none dared resist.

sentences.zh: 事聞之官，刑曹逮鞫服實，竟原其罪。

translations.literal: When the matter reached the authorities, the Penal Bureau arrested and interrogated them; they confessed the facts, yet in the end their crimes were pardoned.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter reached the authorities, the Penal Bureau arrested and interrogated them; they confessed the facts, yet in the end their crimes were pardoned.

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下，肆行無忌，遠在外郡，何事不為！

translations.literal: Under the imperial carriage they act without restraint — in distant outer prefectures, what would they not do!
translations.idiomatic: If they behave so brazenly at the capital itself, what would they not dare in distant prefectures?

sentences.zh: 夫京師天下之本，縱惡如此，何以為政！

translations.literal: The capital is the foundation of the empire; if wickedness is indulged thus, how can there be government!
translations.idiomatic: The capital is the foundation of the empire. If wickedness is indulged in this way, how can the state be governed?

sentences.zh: 古人有言，一婦銜冤，三年不雨，以此論之，即非細務。

translations.literal: The ancients said that when one woman holds a grievance, for three years it does not rain; judged by this, it is no minor affair.
translations.idiomatic: The ancients said that when one woman bears a grievance, rain fails for three years. By that measure, this is no minor affair.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜以即烈、不花付刑曹鞫之。

translations.literal: We propose: Jilie and Buhua should be handed to the Penal Bureau for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that Jilie and Buhua be handed over to the Penal Bureau for trial.

sentences.zh: 中賣寶物，世祖時不聞其事，自成宗以來，始有此弊。

translations.literal: Selling treasures at court — in Shizu's time this was not heard of; from Chengzong onward this abuse began.
translations.idiomatic: The sale of treasures at court was unknown in Shizu's reign; this abuse began only under Chengzong.

sentences.zh: 分珠寸石，售直數万，當時民懷憤怨，台察交言。

translations.literal: Pearls and stones an inch across were sold for tens of thousands; at the time the people nursed anger and resentment, and the censorate spoke in turn.
translations.idiomatic: Pearls and stones no larger than an inch fetched prices in the tens of thousands. The people seethed with anger, and censors protested one after another.

sentences.zh: 且所酬之鈔，率皆天下生民膏血，錙銖取之，從以捶撻，何其用之不吝！

translations.literal: Moreover the paper money paid for them was almost entirely the fat and blood of the people under Heaven — taken bit by bit, often with beating — how lavishly it was spent!
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the paper money paid for these goods was drawn almost entirely from the lifeblood of the people — wrung out coin by coin, often with beatings. How recklessly it was spent!

sentences.zh: 夫以經國有用之寶，而易此不濟飢寒之物，又非有司聘要和買，大抵皆時貴與斡脫中寶之人，妄稱呈獻，冒給回賜，高其直且十倍，蠶蠹國財，暗行分用。

translations.literal: To exchange treasures useful for governing the state for things that cannot relieve hunger or cold — and this was not the regular office purchase at fixed prices — was mostly done when great nobles and the brokers of court treasures falsely claimed presentation, fraudulently received return gifts, inflated the price tenfold, secretly divided the use, and devoured the state's wealth like silkworms.
translations.idiomatic: To exchange state treasures useful for governing the realm for trinkets that cannot feed or clothe anyone — and this was not regular procurement at fixed prices — was mostly the work of great nobles and court treasure brokers who falsely claimed to be presenting gifts, fraudulently received return rewards, inflated prices tenfold, and secretly divided the proceeds, devouring the treasury like silkworms on a leaf.

sentences.zh: 如沙不丁之徒，頃以增價中寶事敗，且存吏牘。

translations.literal: Men such as Shabuding were recently exposed for inflating prices in court treasure sales, and the records still survive.
translations.idiomatic: Men such as Shabuding were recently exposed for inflating prices in court treasure sales, and the records still survive in the archives.

sentences.zh: 陛下即位之初，首知其弊，下令禁止，天下欣幸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Your Majesty's accession you first understood this abuse and issued orders forbidding it; all under Heaven rejoiced.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Your Majesty's reign you recognized this abuse and issued orders to forbid it; the whole empire rejoiced.

sentences.zh: 臣等比聞中書乃復奏給累朝未酬寶價四十餘萬錠，較其元直，利已數倍，有事經年遠者三十餘萬錠，復令給以市舶番貨，計今天下所徵包銀差發，歲入止十一萬錠，已是四年徵入之數，比以經費弗足，急於科徵。

translations.literal: We have lately heard that the Secretariat again memorialized to pay more than four hundred thousand ingots for treasure prices unpaid by successive reigns; compared with the original price the profit is already several times over; some cases stretch back many years for more than three hundred thousand ingots, and payment is again ordered in maritime-trade exotic goods. Counting all the wrapped silver and corvée levies collected under Heaven, annual revenue is only one hundred ten thousand ingots — already four years' intake — yet because funds are insufficient levies are urgently imposed.
translations.idiomatic: We have lately heard that the Secretariat again memorialized to pay more than four hundred thousand ingots in unpaid treasure prices from successive reigns. Compared with the original prices, the markup is already several times over; some claims stretch back many years for more than three hundred thousand ingots, and payment is again to be made in maritime-trade goods. Yet the wrapped silver and corvée levies collected empire-wide yield only one hundred ten thousand ingots a year — the equivalent of four years' revenue — and because funds are insufficient, levies are being imposed with urgency.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：番舶之貨，宜以資國用、紓民力，寶價請俟國用饒給之日議之。

translations.literal: We propose: exotic goods from foreign ships should serve state use and relieve the people's burden; payment of treasure prices should wait until state funds are ample.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that exotic goods from foreign ships be used to support state needs and relieve the people's burden, and that payment of treasure prices wait until the treasury is adequately supplied.

sentences.zh: 太廟神主，祖宗之所妥靈，國家孝治天下，四時大祀，誠為重典。

translations.literal: The spirit tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple are where the ancestors' spirits rest; the state governs the world through filial piety, and the great seasonal sacrifices are truly weighty rites.
translations.idiomatic: The spirit tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple are where the ancestors' spirits rest. The state governs through filial piety, and the great seasonal sacrifices are truly solemn rites.

sentences.zh: 比者仁宗皇帝、皇后神主，盜利其金而竊之，至今未獲。

translations.literal: Recently the spirit tablets of Emperor Renzong and the Empress were stolen for their gold; they have not yet been recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Recently the spirit tablets of Emperor Renzong and the Empress were stolen for their gold, and they have not yet been recovered.

sentences.zh: 斯乃非常之事，而捕盜官兵，不聞杖責。

translations.literal: This is an extraordinary matter, yet among the officers and soldiers who hunt thieves, none has heard of beating or punishment.
translations.idiomatic: This is an extraordinary crime, yet none of the officers and soldiers charged with catching thieves has faced beating or punishment.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：庶民失盜，應捕官兵，尚有三限之法；

translations.literal: We propose: when common people suffer theft, the officers who should catch thieves still have the three-deadline law;
translations.idiomatic: We propose: when common people suffer theft, the officers charged with catching thieves are still subject to the three-deadline law;

sentences.zh: 監臨主守，倘失官物，亦有不行知覺之罪。

translations.literal: supervisors and custodians who lose official goods also have the crime of failing to detect it.
translations.idiomatic: and supervisors and custodians who lose official goods are also liable for failing to detect the loss.

sentences.zh: 今失神主，宜罪太常，請揀其官屬免之。

translations.literal: Now that spirit tablets have been lost, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices should be punished; we ask that its officials be selected and dismissed.
translations.idiomatic: Now that spirit tablets have been lost, the Court of Imperial Sacrifices should be held accountable; we ask that its officials be selected and dismissed.

sentences.zh: 國家經賦，皆出於民，量入為出，有司之事。

translations.literal: The state's taxes and levies all come from the people; measuring income to set expenditure is the business of the offices.
translations.idiomatic: The state's taxes and levies all come from the people; measuring income against expenditure is the duty of the offices.

sentences.zh: 比者建西山寺，損軍害民，費以億萬計；

translations.literal: Recently in building the Western Hills Temple, troops were harmed and the people injured, at a cost reckoned in hundreds of millions;
translations.idiomatic: Recently, in building the Western Hills Temple, troops were harmed and the people burdened, at a cost reckoned in the hundreds of millions;

sentences.zh: 刺繡經幡，馳驛江浙，逼迫郡縣，雜役男女，動經年歲，窮奢致怨。

translations.literal: embroidered sutra banners were rushed by post relay through Jiang and Zhe, pressing prefectures and counties, conscripting men and women in mixed labor for years on end, exhausting luxury arousing resentment.
translations.idiomatic: embroidered sutra banners were rushed by post relay through Jiangsu and Zhejiang, pressing prefectures and counties to conscript men and women in mixed labor for years on end — extravagance that bred widespread resentment.

sentences.zh: 近詔雖已罷之，又聞奸人乘間奏請，复欲興修，流言喧播，群情驚駭。

translations.literal: Though a recent edict has already stopped this, we again hear that wicked men seize the interval to memorialize, wishing once more to undertake construction; rumors spread and the people's feelings are alarmed and terrified.
translations.idiomatic: Although a recent edict has already halted this work, we again hear that wicked men are seizing the moment to memorialize for renewed construction; rumors are spreading and the people are alarmed and terrified.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜守前詔，示民有信，其創造、刺繡事，非歲用之常者，悉罷之。

translations.literal: We propose: the earlier edict should be upheld to show the people good faith; construction and embroidery work that are not regular annual expenditure should all be stopped.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that the earlier edict be upheld to show the people that the throne keeps its word, and that construction and embroidery projects that are not part of regular annual expenditure be stopped entirely.

sentences.zh: 人有冤抑，必當昭雪，事有枉直，尤宜明辨。

translations.literal: When people suffer wrongful oppression, it must be redressed; when affairs are crooked or straight, they should especially be clearly distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: When people suffer wrongful oppression, justice must be done; when right and wrong are at stake, the distinction must be made clear.

sentences.zh: 平章政事蕭拜住、中丞楊朵兒只等，枉遭鐵木迭兒誣陷，籍其家以分賜人，聞者嗟悼。

translations.literal: Grand Councilor Xiao Baizhu, Censor-in-Chief Yang Duerzhi, and others were wrongfully slandered and trapped by Temuder; their households were registered and divided as gifts to others — those who heard sighed in grief.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Councilor Xiao Baizhu, Censor-in-Chief Yang Duerzhi, and others were wrongfully framed by Temuder; their households were confiscated and divided as gifts to others — all who heard of it mourned.

sentences.zh: 比奉明詔，還給元業，子孫奉祀家廟，修葺苟完，未及寧處，復以其家財仍賜舊人，止酬以直，即與再罹斷沒無異。

translations.literal: Recently by clear edict their original estates were returned, their descendants maintained the ancestral temple, and repairs were barely finished before they could settle — yet their household wealth was again granted to the old recipients, compensated only at market price, no different from suffering confiscation a second time.
translations.idiomatic: Recently, by clear edict their original estates were restored, their descendants were to maintain the ancestral temple, and repairs were barely finished before they could settle — yet their household wealth was again granted to the old recipients, with compensation only at market price, no different from suffering confiscation a second time.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜如前詔，以元業還之，量其直以酬後所賜者，則人無冤憤矣。

translations.literal: We propose: as in the earlier edict, the original estates should be returned, and the later grantees compensated at fair value — then people will have no grievance or anger.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that, as in the earlier edict, the original estates be returned and the later grantees compensated at fair value — then no one will harbor grievance or anger.

sentences.zh: 德以出治，刑以防奸。

translations.literal: Virtue brings forth good government; punishment guards against wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: Virtue brings forth good government; punishment guards against wickedness.

sentences.zh: 若刑罰不立，姦宄滋長，雖有智者，不能禁止。

translations.literal: If punishments are not established, wickedness grows; even the wise cannot restrain it.
translations.idiomatic: If punishments are not enforced, wickedness proliferates; even the wise cannot restrain it.

sentences.zh: 比者也先鐵木兒之徒，遇硃太醫妻女過省門外，強拽以入，姦宿館所。

translations.literal: Recently Yesun Temur and his kind, meeting Physician Zhu's wife and daughter passing outside the provincial gate, forcibly dragged them in and raped them at the lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Yesun Temur and his followers, encountering Physician Zhu's wife and daughter passing outside the provincial gate, forcibly dragged them inside and raped them at the lodge.

sentences.zh: 事聞，有司以扈從上都為解，竟弗就鞫。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported, the office excused them on the ground of escorting the court to the Upper Capital, and in the end they were not interrogated.
translations.idiomatic: When the matter was reported, the authorities excused them on the ground that they were escorting the court to the Upper Capital, and in the end they were never brought to trial.

sentences.zh: 輦轂之下，肆惡無忌，京民憤駭，何以取則四方！

translations.literal: Under the imperial carriage they commit wickedness without restraint; the capital's people are angry and terrified — how can this serve as a model for the four directions!
translations.idiomatic: Under the imperial carriage they commit wickedness without restraint; the people of the capital are furious and terrified — how can this serve as a model for the whole empire?

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜遵世祖成憲，以奸人命有司鞫之。

translations.literal: We propose: Shizu's established statutes should be followed, and the criminals handed to the proper offices for interrogation.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that Shizu's established statutes be followed and the criminals handed over to the proper offices for trial.

sentences.zh: 臣等又議：天下囚系，冤滯不無，方今盛夏，宜命省台選官審錄，結正重刑，疏決輕系，疑者申聞詳讞。

translations.literal: We further propose: among prisoners under Heaven, wrongful detention is not absent; now at the height of summer, provincial and censorial offices should be ordered to select officials to review cases, finalize heavy sentences, release lighter detainees, and refer doubtful cases upward for detailed judgment.
translations.idiomatic: We further propose that, since wrongful detention is not unknown among prisoners empire-wide, and summer is now at its height, provincial and censorial offices be ordered to select officials to review cases — finalize heavy sentences, release lighter detainees, and refer doubtful cases upward for detailed judgment.

sentences.zh: 邊鎮利病，宜命行省、行台體究興除，廣海鎮戍卒更病者，給粥食藥；

translations.literal: The strengths and weaknesses of border garrisons should be investigated by branch secretariats and censorates for what to establish or abolish; garrison soldiers on the Guang coast who fall ill on rotation should be given gruel, food, and medicine;
translations.idiomatic: The strengths and weaknesses of border garrisons should be investigated by branch secretariats and censorates for what to establish or abolish; garrison soldiers on the Guang coast who fall ill during rotation should be given gruel, food, and medicine;

sentences.zh: 力死者，人給鈔二十五貫，責所司及同鄉者，歸骨於其家。

translations.literal: those who die from overwork should receive twenty-five strings of paper money each; the responsible office and men of the same native place should return the bones to their families.
translations.idiomatic: and those who die from overwork should receive twenty-five strings of paper money each, with the responsible office and men of the same native place charged to return their remains to their families.

sentences.zh: 歲貢方物有常制。

translations.literal: Tribute of regional products has fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Tribute of regional products follows fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 廣州東​​莞縣大步海及惠州珠池，始自大德元年，奸民劉進、程連言利，分蜑戶七百餘家，官給之糧，三年一採，僅獲小珠五兩六兩，入水為蟲魚傷死者眾，遂罷珠戶為民。

translations.literal: At Dabu Sea in Dongguan County, Guangzhou, and at the pearl pools of Huizhou — beginning in the first year of Dade, wicked men Liu Jin and Cheng Lian spoke of profit, divided more than seven hundred Tanka households, supplied them with grain by the state, and harvested pearls once every three years — only five or six taels of small pearls were obtained; many died from insect and fish wounds in the water, and the pearl households were abolished and made commoners.
translations.idiomatic: At Dabu Sea in Dongguan County, Guangzhou, and at the pearl pools of Huizhou — beginning in Dade 1, wicked men Liu Jin and Cheng Lian spoke of profit, divided more than seven hundred Tanka households, supplied them with state grain, and harvested pearls once every three years — yet only five or six taels of small pearls were obtained. Many drowned workers died from insect and fish wounds, and the pearl households were abolished and restored to common status.

sentences.zh: 其後同知廣州路事塔塔兒等，又獻利於失列門，創設提舉司監採，廉訪司言其擾民，复罷歸有司。

translations.literal: Later Associate Administrator of the Guangzhou Circuit Tatar and others again presented profit to Shiremen, established a supervisory office for pearl gathering, and the surveillance commission said it harassed the people — it was again abolished and returned to the regular offices.
translations.idiomatic: Later, Associate Administrator of the Guangzhou Circuit Tatar and others again presented the scheme as profitable to Shiremen, established a supervisory office for pearl gathering, and the surveillance commission reported that it harassed the people — whereupon it was again abolished and returned to the regular offices.

sentences.zh: 既而內正少卿魏暗都剌，冒啟中旨，馳驛督採，耗廩食，疲民驛，非舊制，請悉罷遣歸民。

translations.literal: Then Vice Director of the Inner Palace Wei Edula falsely obtained an inner edict, rushed by post relay to supervise gathering, wasted granary provisions, and exhausted the people and post stations — not the old system; we ask that all be abolished and the people returned to their livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Then Vice Director of the Inner Palace Wei Edula falsely obtained an inner edict, rushed by post relay to supervise gathering, wasted granary provisions, and exhausted the people and post stations — contrary to the old system. We ask that all such operations be abolished and the people returned to their livelihoods.

sentences.zh: 善良死於非命，國法當為昭雪。

translations.literal: When the good die by violence, state law should redress it.
translations.idiomatic: When the innocent die by violence, the law of the state should bring them justice.

sentences.zh: 鐵失弒逆之變，學士不花、指揮不顏忽裡、院使禿古思皆以無罪死，未褒贈；

translations.literal: In Tieshi's treacherous regicide, Academician Buhua, Commander Buyan Khuli, and Court Director Tugusi all died though guiltless, and have not yet received posthumous honors;
translations.idiomatic: In Tieshi's treacherous regicide, Academician Buhua, Commander Buyan Khuli, and Court Director Tugusi all died though guiltless, and have not yet received posthumous honors;

sentences.zh: 鐵木迭兒專權之際，御史徐元素以言事鎖項死東平，及買禿堅不花之屬，皆未申理。

translations.literal: during Temuder's monopoly of power, Censor Xu Yuansu died with a cangue on his neck at Dongping for speaking out, and men such as Mai Tujian Buhua have not yet had their cases reviewed.
translations.idiomatic: during Temuder's monopoly of power, Censor Xu Yuansu died in a cangue at Dongping for speaking out, and men such as Mai Tujian Buhua have not yet had their cases reviewed.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜追贈死者，優敘其子孫，且命刑部及監察御史，體勘其餘有冤抑者，具實以聞。

translations.literal: We propose: the dead should receive posthumous honors, their descendants should receive preferential treatment, and the Ministry of Justice and the surveillance censors should investigate the rest who suffer wrongful oppression and report the facts.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that the dead receive posthumous honors, their descendants receive preferential treatment, and the Ministry of Justice and the surveillance censors investigate others who suffer wrongful oppression and report the facts.

sentences.zh: 政出多門，古人所戒。

translations.literal: When government issues from many gates, the ancients warned against it.
translations.idiomatic: When government issues from many gates, the ancients warned against it.

sentences.zh: 今內外增置官署，員冗俸濫，白丁驟升出身，入流壅塞日甚，軍民俱蒙其害。

translations.literal: Now inner and outer offices are added in number; posts are redundant and salaries excessive; raw recruits are suddenly promoted into office; entry into the regular ranks is blocked daily; soldiers and civilians both suffer harm.
translations.idiomatic: Now offices are being added throughout the government; posts are redundant and salaries excessive; raw recruits are suddenly promoted into office; entry into the regular ranks grows more blocked by the day; and both soldiers and civilians suffer.

sentences.zh: 夫為治之要，莫先於安民；

translations.literal: The key to governing lies first in settling the people;
translations.idiomatic: The key to governing lies first in settling the people;

sentences.zh: 安民之道，莫急於除濫費、汰冗員。

translations.literal: the way to settle the people lies first in removing wasteful spending and cutting redundant posts.
translations.idiomatic: and the way to settle the people lies first in removing wasteful spending and cutting redundant posts.

sentences.zh: 世祖設官分職，俱有定制。

translations.literal: When Shizu established offices and divided duties, all had fixed regulations.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizu established offices and divided duties, all had fixed regulations.

sentences.zh: 至元三十年已後，改升創設，日積月增，雖嘗奉旨取勘減降，近侍各私其署，夤緣保祿，姑息中止。

translations.literal: After the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan, promotions and new establishments accumulated month by month; though orders were once issued to investigate and reduce them, each palace favorite protected his own office, pulled strings to preserve salaries, and indulgence stopped the effort midway.
translations.idiomatic: After Zhiyuan 30, promotions and new establishments accumulated month by month. Though orders were once issued to investigate and reduce them, each palace favorite protected his own office, pulled strings to preserve salaries, and indulgence halted the effort midway.

sentences.zh: 至英宗時，始銳然減罷崇祥、壽福院之屬十有三署，徽政院斷事官、江淮財賦之屬六十餘署，不幸遭罹大故，未竟其餘。

translations.literal: Only in Emperor Yingzong's time was there a sharp reduction and abolition of thirteen offices such as the Chongxiang and Shoufu courts, and more than sixty offices such as the Huizheng Court's judicial officers and the Jiang-Huai revenue offices — but unfortunately a great calamity befell, and the rest was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: Only under Emperor Yingzong was there a sharp reduction and abolition of thirteen offices such as the Chongxiang and Shoufu courts, and more than sixty offices such as the Huizheng Court's judicial officers and the Jiang-Huai revenue offices — but unfortunately a great calamity intervened, and the rest was never completed.

sentences.zh: 比奉詔：凡事悉遵世祖成憲。

translations.literal: Recently an edict was received: in all matters fully follow Shizu's established statutes.
translations.idiomatic: Recently an edict was received: in all matters fully follow Shizu's established statutes.

sentences.zh: 若復循常取勘，調虛文，延歲月，必無實效，即與詔旨異矣。

translations.literal: If we again follow routine investigation, adjust empty documents, and delay months and years, there will surely be no real effect — that would differ from the edict's intent.
translations.idiomatic: If we again follow routine investigation, shuffle empty documents, and delay month after month, there will surely be no real effect — that would contradict the edict's intent.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜敕中外軍民，署置官吏，有非世祖之制，及至元三十年已後改升創設員冗者，詔格至日，悉減並除罷之；

translations.literal: We propose: civil and military offices throughout inner and outer government — any not of Shizu's system, and any redundant posts promoted or newly established after the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan — from the day of the edict should all be reduced, merged, and abolished;
translations.idiomatic: We propose that civil and military offices throughout the government — any not of Shizu's system, and any redundant posts promoted or newly established after Zhiyuan 30 — from the day of the edict be reduced, merged, and abolished;

sentences.zh: 近侍不得巧詞复奏，不該常調之人亦不得濫入常選。

translations.literal: palace favorites must not craft words to memorialize again, and persons not eligible for regular appointment must not enter the regular selection.
translations.idiomatic: that palace favorites must not craft pretexts to memorialize again, and that persons not eligible for regular appointment must not enter the regular selection.

sentences.zh: 累朝斡耳朵所立長秋、承徽、長寧寺及邊鎮屯戍，別議處之。

translations.literal: The Changqiu, Chenghui, and Changning temples established at the ordos of successive reigns, and border garrison colonies, should be dealt with separately.
translations.idiomatic: The Changqiu, Chenghui, and Changning temples established at the ordos of successive reigns, and border garrison colonies, should be dealt with separately.

sentences.zh: 自古聖君，惟誠於治政，可以動天地、感鬼神，初未嘗徼福於僧道，以厲民病國也。

translations.literal: Since ancient times sage rulers have moved Heaven and touched spirits only through sincerity in governing — they never sought blessing from monks and Daoists to afflict the people and harm the state.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times, sage rulers have moved Heaven and touched spirits only through sincerity in governing — they never sought blessing from monks and Daoists at the cost of afflicting the people and harming the state.

sentences.zh: 且以至元三十年言之，醮祠佛事之目，止百有二。

translations.literal: Take the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan: the items for Daoist rites and Buddhist services numbered only one hundred and two.
translations.idiomatic: Take Zhiyuan 30: the items for Daoist rites and Buddhist services numbered only one hundred and two.

sentences.zh: 大德七年，再立功德使司，積五百有餘，今年一增其目，明年即指為例，已倍四之上矣。

translations.literal: In the seventh year of Dade the Merit Office was re-established; they accumulated to more than five hundred; one year an item was added, the next it was cited as precedent — already more than four times the former number.
translations.idiomatic: In Dade 7 the Merit Office was re-established; the items accumulated to more than five hundred. One year a new item was added, the next it was cited as precedent — already more than four times the former number.

sentences.zh: 僧徒又復營幹近侍，買作佛事，指以算卦，欺昧奏請，增修布施莽齋，自稱特奉、傳奉，所司不敢較問，供給恐後。

translations.literal: Monks again cultivated palace favorites, bought Buddhist services, pointed to divination, deceived in memorializing, increased offerings and lavish feasts, called themselves specially commissioned or transmitted commission — the offices dared not compare or question, fearing to lag in supply.
translations.idiomatic: Monks again cultivated palace favorites, purchased Buddhist services, invoked divination, deceived in their memorials, increased offerings and lavish feasts, and styled themselves specially commissioned or transmitted commission — the offices dared not challenge them, fearing to fall behind in supply.

sentences.zh: 況佛以清淨為本，不奔不欲，而僧徒貪慕貨利，自違其教，一事所需，金銀鈔幣不可數計，歲用鈔數千萬錠，數倍於至元間矣。

translations.literal: Moreover the Buddha takes purity as root, not running after desires — yet monks greedily covet goods and profit, themselves violating their teaching; for a single affair gold, silver, and paper money cannot be counted; annual use is tens of millions of ingots — several times that of the Zhiyuan period.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Buddha takes purity as his root and does not run after desires — yet monks greedily covet wealth, violating their own teaching. A single affair consumes gold, silver, and paper money beyond counting; annual expenditure runs to tens of millions of ingots — several times that of the Zhiyuan period.

sentences.zh: 凡所供物，悉為己有，布施等鈔，復出其外，生民脂膏，縱其所欲，取以自利，畜養妻子，彼既行不修潔，適足褻慢天神，何以要福！

translations.literal: All goods supplied they kept for themselves; offering money was extra beyond that; the people's fat and grease they took at will for their own profit, rearing wives and children — they themselves behave without purity, sufficient only to profane Heaven — how can they seek blessing!
translations.idiomatic: All goods supplied they kept for themselves; offering money was extra on top of that. They took the people's lifeblood at will for their own profit, rearing wives and children — behaving without purity themselves, sufficient only to profane Heaven. How can they seek blessing?

sentences.zh: 比年佛事愈繁，累朝享國不永，致災愈速，事無應驗，斷可知矣。

translations.literal: In recent years Buddhist affairs grow ever more numerous; successive reigns' tenure of the realm was not long; disasters come ever faster; affairs find no response — this can clearly be known.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years Buddhist affairs grow ever more numerous; successive reigns have not long held the realm; disasters arrive ever faster; and the rites find no response — the conclusion is plain.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜罷功德使司，其在至元三十年以前及累朝忌日醮祠佛事名目，止令宣政院主領修舉，餘悉減罷，近侍之屬，並不得巧計擅奏，妄增名目；

translations.literal: We propose: the Merit Office should be abolished; for items of Daoist rites and Buddhist services before the thirtieth year of Zhiyuan and on successive reigns' memorial days, only the Xuanzheng Court should preside — the rest should all be reduced and stopped; palace favorites must not by crafty schemes memorialize on their own authority or falsely add items;
translations.idiomatic: We propose that the Merit Office be abolished; that for Daoist rites and Buddhist services before Zhiyuan 30 and on successive reigns' memorial days, only the Xuanzheng Court preside — the rest be reduced and stopped; and that palace favorites must not by crafty schemes memorialize on their own authority or falsely add items;

sentences.zh: 若有特奉、傳奉，從中書復奏乃行。

translations.literal: if there are specially commissioned or transmitted commissions, the Secretariat must memorialize again before they proceed.
translations.idiomatic: and that any specially commissioned or transmitted commission must be memorialized again through the Secretariat before it may proceed.

sentences.zh: 古今帝王治國理財之要，莫先於節用，蓋侈用則傷財，傷財必至於害民；

translations.literal: The key to governing the state and managing finances for emperors ancient and modern lies first in frugality — for extravagant use injures wealth, and injured wealth must reach the point of harming the people;
translations.idiomatic: For emperors ancient and modern, the key to governing the state and managing finances lies first in frugality — for extravagant spending drains the treasury, and a drained treasury inevitably harms the people;

sentences.zh: 國用匱而重斂生，如鹽課增價之類，皆足以厲民矣。

translations.literal: when state funds are exhausted heavy levies arise — such as raising salt tax prices — all sufficient to afflict the people.
translations.idiomatic: when state funds are exhausted, heavy levies follow — such as raising salt tax prices — all of which afflict the people.

sentences.zh: 比年遊惰之徒，妄投宿衛部屬及宦者、女紅、太醫、陰陽之屬，不可勝數，一人收籍，一門蠲复，一歲所請衣馬芻糧，數十戶所徵入不足以給之，耗國損民為甚。

translations.literal: In recent years idle men have rashly enrolled in the imperial guard, eunuchs, palace women, imperial physicians, yin-yang masters, and the like beyond counting; one man's registration frees a whole household from corvée; clothing, horses, fodder, and grain requested in a year — the intake of several tens of households is insufficient to supply it — wasting the state and harming the people greatly.
translations.idiomatic: In recent years idle men have rashly enrolled in the imperial guard, eunuchs, palace women, imperial physicians, yin-yang masters, and the like beyond counting. One man's registration frees an entire household from corvée; the clothing, horses, fodder, and grain requested in a year exceed what several tens of households pay in taxes — greatly wasting state resources and harming the people.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：諸宿衛宦女之屬，宜如世祖時支請之數給之，餘悉簡汰。

translations.literal: We propose: for the imperial guard, eunuchs, palace women, and the like, payment should follow the numbers given in Shizu's time; the rest should all be screened and cut.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that for the imperial guard, eunuchs, palace women, and the like, payment follow the numbers given in Shizu's time, and that the rest be screened and cut.

sentences.zh: 闊端赤牧養馬駝，歲有常法，分佈郡縣，各有常數，而宿衛近侍，委之僕禦，役民放牧。

translations.literal: Imperial stud horses and camels are pastured by annual fixed law, distributed among prefectures and counties each with fixed numbers — yet the imperial guard and palace favorites entrust them to grooms and servants who press the people to pasture them.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial stud horses and camels are pastured under fixed annual regulations, distributed among prefectures and counties each with fixed quotas — yet the imperial guard and palace favorites entrust them to grooms and servants who press the people to pasture them.

sentences.zh: 始至，即奪其居，俾飲食之，殘傷桑果，百害蜂起；

translations.literal: As soon as they arrive they seize people's dwellings, make them provide food and drink, damage mulberry trees and fruit — a hundred harms swarm forth;
translations.idiomatic: As soon as they arrive they seize people's dwellings, make them provide food and drink, and damage mulberry trees and fruit — a hundred harms swarm forth;

sentences.zh: 其僕禦四出，無所拘鈐，私鬻芻豆，瘠損馬駝。

translations.literal: their grooms and servants go out in all directions without restraint, privately selling fodder and beans, emaciating horses and camels.
translations.idiomatic: their grooms and servants roam in all directions without restraint, privately selling fodder and beans and emaciating the horses and camels.

sentences.zh: 大德中，始責州縣正官監視，蓋暖棚、團槽櫪以牧之。

translations.literal: In the Dade period, prefectural and county chief officials were first charged with supervision — warm sheds and round mangers were built for pasturing.
translations.idiomatic: In the Dade period, prefectural and county chief officials were first charged with supervision — warm sheds and round mangers were built for pasturing.

sentences.zh: 至治初，复散之民間，其害如故。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhizhi they were again scattered among the people; the harm was as before.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Zhizhi they were again scattered among the people; the harm was as before.

sentences.zh: 監察御史及河間路守臣屢言之。

translations.literal: Surveillance censors and the Hejian Circuit officials have repeatedly spoken of this.
translations.idiomatic: Surveillance censors and the officials of Hejian Circuit have repeatedly reported this.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：宜如大德團槽之制，正官監臨，閱視肥瘠，拘鈐宿衛僕禦，著為令。

translations.literal: We propose: the Dade round-manger system should be followed, with chief officials supervising, inspecting fat and lean, restraining the grooms and servants of the imperial guard — and this should be established as law.
translations.idiomatic: We propose that the Dade round-manger system be restored, with chief officials supervising, inspecting the condition of the animals, and restraining the grooms and servants of the imperial guard — and that this be established as law.

sentences.zh: 兵戎之興，號為凶器，擅開邊釁，非國之福。

translations.literal: When arms are raised they are called baleful instruments; to open border provocation without authority is no blessing to the state.
translations.idiomatic: Arms are called baleful instruments; to provoke border conflict without authority is no blessing to the state.

sentences.zh: 蠻夷無知，少梗王化，得之無益，失之無損。

translations.literal: Barbarians are ignorant; if they slightly obstruct royal transformation, gaining them is without benefit, losing them is without loss.
translations.idiomatic: Barbarians are ignorant; if they slightly obstruct royal civilization, gaining them brings no benefit and losing them brings no loss.

sentences.zh: 至治三年，參卜郎盜，始者劫殺使臣，利其財物而已。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhizhi, the Canbolang bandits at first only robbed and killed envoys for their goods.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhizhi 3, the Canbolang bandits at first robbed and killed envoys only for their goods.

sentences.zh: 至用大師，期年不戢，傷我士卒，費國資糧。

translations.literal: The Zhiyong campaign lasted a year without restraint, wounding our soldiers and wasting state funds and grain.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhiyong campaign lasted a year without success, wounding our soldiers and wasting state funds and grain.

sentences.zh: 臣等議：好生惡死，人之恆性。

translations.literal: We propose: cherishing life and hating death is the constant nature of human beings.
translations.idiomatic: We propose: cherishing life and hating death is the constant nature of human beings.

sentences.zh: 宜令宣政院督守將嚴邊防，遣良使抵巢招諭。

translations.literal: The Xuanzheng Court should be ordered to supervise border generals in strict frontier defense, and to send good envoys to their lairs to summon and instruct them.
translations.idiomatic: The Xuanzheng Court should be ordered to supervise border generals in strict frontier defense and to send capable envoys to their strongholds to summon and instruct them.

sentences.zh: 簡罷冗兵，明敕邊吏謹守禦，勿生事，則遠人格矣。
